headline: PM Tarique Rahman vows to crush conspiracies during National Revolution Day rally
summary: Leading thousands in a massive procession through Dhaka, the Prime Minister warns that no force can suppress the democratic aspirations of the people.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman led a massive 'Sovereignty' procession in Dhaka on Saturday to observe National Revolution and Solidarity Day. This marks the first time the BNP-led government has celebrated the day in nearly 20 years.

Addressing the crowd at Nayapaltan, the Prime Minister warned against internal and external conspiracies, vowing to give a 'tooth-breaking' response to any attempt to undermine the country's democracy.
He emphasized that just as oppressive forces were defeated on November 7, 1975, and during the mass uprising of August 5, 2024, any current attempts to suppress the people will fail.
Tarique Rahman criticized attempts to reinstate 'dummy elections' and asserted that the people who brought about the 1971 liberation and the 2024 uprising cannot be silenced.
During the rally, the Prime Minister chanted slogans emphasizing Bangladesh's sovereignty, stating 'Not Delhi, not Pindi, but Bangladesh first, Bangladesh for all.'

The procession started from the BNP central office in Nayapaltan and passed through Kakrail, Farmgate, and Bijoy Sarani, ending at Manik Mia Avenue, with thousands of supporters carrying national flags and party placards.
The event was attended by several cabinet ministers, including Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, along with other senior party leaders.

headline_marked: 2 buses caught fire in [[two separate incidents in Dhaka]] in one night
headline: 2 buses caught fire in two separate incidents in Dhaka in one night
summary: A Shohag Paribahan bus at Mohakhali terminal and a Bihanga Paribahan bus in Mirpur were targeted in separate fire incidents on Saturday night and Sunday morning.
details: Two passenger buses were caught fire in the capital within a single night, marking a series of alarming incidents in different parts of the city.
A Shohag Paribahan bus parked at the Mohakhali bus terminal caught fire shortly before 1am on Sunday. Two units from the Tejgaon Fire Station were dispatched to the scene to control the flames.

Earlier on Saturday night, a Bihanga Paribahan bus was targeted in Mirpur around 10pm. Police report that attackers on a motorcycle poured petrol through a window onto the rear section of the parked bus and set it alight.
Bus staff managed to extinguish the fire in Mirpur, preventing a larger disaster, but several seats at the back of the vehicle were damaged.
Authorities are investigating the cause of the fire at Mohakhali and the cause of the arson attack in Mirpur.
